speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg; to help me understand your condition, can you tell me how long this lesion has been present and if you notice any redness, warmth, or swelling around it?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (secondary to ant bite) or Pyoderma Gangrenosum (due to Crohn's/Neutrophilic dermatosis) given the ulcerative nature, rapid progression, and history of immune suppression from uveitis treatment and diabetes. I will request a skin biopsy and wound culture to differentiate between infectious etiology and neutrophilic dermatosis. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy; REQUEST TEST: Wound_Culture.
